Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:28: Therefore a voice goes forth every night, when the Holy One, blessed be He, descends into the Garden of Eden, when souls ascend before Him, and that voice says "proclaim," as it is written (Isaiah 40:6), "a voice says, proclaim" — go and tell them to engage in Torah to unite the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the manner of David, who said (Psalms 132:4), "I will not give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids, until I find a place for the Lord" — and he would engage in Torah to unite the Mother, of whom it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "and do not forsake the Torah of your mother," with her husband — for the Shechinah, from the side of Chesed, is called "acts of lovingkindness," and from the side of Gevurah is called "binding [akedah] and sacrifice," and from the side of the central pillar is called "Torah" — and there is none to arouse her toward her husband through these attributes; this is what is written (Isaiah 51:18), "there is none to guide her," etc. Therefore the voice says: what shall I proclaim? "All flesh is grass" — for they strive only to slaughter flesh, and these are the ignorant common folk.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:29: And those who strive in acts of lovingkindness and in Torah, but strive only for themselves, of them it is said (Isaiah 40:6), "and all his kindness is like the flower of the field" — and all these who do not engage in it for its own sake, the holy spirit, which is the Shechinah, does not rest upon them, this being what is written (Psalms 78:39), "and He remembered that they were flesh, a spirit that goes and does not return," etc. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:30: Here is explained the great obligation upon students of Torah, that their intent should be to unify the Shechinah, and not their intent be for their own benefit, to attain wisdom or reward in the World to Come — for regarding this the Shechinah protests and says, "and all his kindness is like the flower of the field," as it says, "and those who strive in acts of lovingkindness and in Torah strive only for themselves."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:31: All this is included in a person striving to be called a son and not a servant — for a son simply serves without intending to receive reward, whereas one who serves in order to receive reward is punished; and it is explained in the Tikkunim (73b), in these words: fear and love performed in order to receive reward are a maidservant, and "under three things the earth trembles," etc., "under a servant when he becomes king, and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress" (Proverbs 30:21-23).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:32: Further, in the Tikkunim (14b), regarding the obligation of the Oral Torah to unify, in these words: happy are those who engage with the Shechinah, who is above all, through halachah, to bring her out of exile, of whom it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away," and to bring her to her husband, that she be received in his arms, to fulfill in her (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," etc. — for in exile the "second-in-command," who is Metatron, rules in exile, and he is a viceroy to the King, in the place where the Queen should sit the viceroy sits — this is "a maidservant when she supplants her mistress." And in the days of Moses the maidservant did not rule, but rather the Queen; but after Moses died and Joshua inherited, who is a "youth" in the place of kingship, the maidservant ruled, as it is said (Joshua 5:14), "I am the captain of the host of the Lord; now I have come" — and we have already established this. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:33: Regarding the warning to engage in Torah, we are commanded in parashat Va'ahavta (Deuteronomy 6:6), "and these words which I command you today shall be upon your heart" — so that they be upon his heart, meaning that he engage in them from his heart and from his soul. "And you shall teach them diligently [sharpen them] to your children" — our sages, of blessed memory, explained that words of Torah should be sharp in your mouth. And it says afterward, "and you shall speak of them" — our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yoma 19b), "and you shall speak of them" — make them a fixed practice. "When you sit in your house, and when you walk on the road, and when you lie down, and when you rise" — these are four times for engaging in Torah, so that one is never free of words of Torah even for a single hour. And just as Torah is a tree of life and is the essential means of clinging to the supernal life, as explained at the beginning of parashat Va'etchanan (Zohar 260a): a person's counsel in this world should be that he strive to engage in Torah day and night without ever departing from it, this being what is written (Joshua 1:8), "and you shall meditate on it day and night" — woe to one who departs from Torah or separates from it, as though he departed and separated from life itself. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:34: Also through engaging in Torah the Shechinah is unified above, and through her the union and love between her and the Holy One, blessed be He, are aroused; and engaging in Torah is the primary means of arousal of the "female waters," as explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayikra 22a), in these words: come and see, the secret of the matter — the Assembly of Israel does not stand before the King except through Torah, for as long as Israel are in the land engaged in Torah, the Assembly of Israel dwells with them; when they cease from words of Torah, she cannot remain with them even for a moment. Therefore, at the time the Assembly of Israel is aroused toward the King, her strength is strengthened, and the Holy King rejoices to receive them; but whenever the Assembly of Israel comes to the King and Torah is not found with her, so to speak her strength weakens — woe to those who weaken the power above! Therefore happy are those who engage in Torah. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:35: Similarly, it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Va'etchanan 268a) on the verse (Deuteronomy 30:20), "for He is your life and the length of your days, to dwell on the land" — explained there that the Shechinah stands and settles neither above nor below except through engaging in Torah. And it says: I found this secret in the book of Rav Hamnuna Sabba, and he established the verse as referring to the secret of the Assembly of Israel, as it is written (Exodus 21:10), "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" — and if these are withheld from her, what is written (ibid. 21:11)? "Then she shall go out free, without payment" — as it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "where is your mother's bill of divorce, whom I sent away"; and it is written (ibid. 52:3), "you were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money." And whoever withholds Torah from her is like one who takes a man's wife and withholds her from him, for she remains like a widow who is not [really] a widow — this being what is written (Lamentations 1:1), "she has become like a widow," and not [truly] a widow. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:36: Here it is explicitly stated that Torah has three levels not found in the other commandments — namely, "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights" — and this is what is meant by "whoever withholds Torah is like one who takes a man's wife" — separating her husband from her, for a husband gives his wife food, clothing, and conjugal rights, and conjugal rights, being the distress of the body, is greater than all — therefore the Shechinah is rectified through Torah more than through all the other commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 8:37: The study of Torah is one commandment among the commandments of the Torah, except that it is all-encompassing and more inward than all the rest — for study leads to action, that one fulfill all the other commandments, and without study there is no [proper] action, as elaborated at length in the Sifrei; we shall quote their words in the next Gate, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:1: Since in the previous chapter we explained that a person is obligated to unify the Shechinah always, in all his affairs, as it is said (Proverbs 3:6), "in all your ways know Him," we wish in this chapter to further explain several particulars that a person is obligated to do out of love for the Shechinah, and through this the Shechinah will find some rest, a place in which to dwell. We have already quoted above, in the previous chapter, the statement of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, that all six weekdays she goes wandering from place to place and from location to location, to see whether she can find a righteous man to whom she may cling.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:2: When a person does all his affairs for the rectification of the Shechinah, who is his mother, it follows that he is a son who brings contentment to his mother, and this is the rank of the masters of Kabbalah, of whom it is said (Deuteronomy 22:6), "you shall not take the mother with the sons" — and it is explained in the Tikkunim that the intent is, do not remove the Shechinah from over the sons, for she is always with them. And it says, in these words (4a): eggs belong to masters of Scripture, chicks to masters of Mishnah, sons to masters of Kabbalah — and of them it is said (Deuteronomy 22:6), "and the mother sitting upon the chicks or upon the eggs, you shall surely send away" from them; but regarding the masters of Kabbalah it is said, "do not take the mother with the sons" — for there is no understanding that recognizes the Shechinah like these masters of Kabbalah, and these make Him, the Holy One, blessed be He, a dwelling, and fly with her wherever she flies — all of them wander with her in her banishment. But the chicks' wings are not whole enough to fly with, these being the positive commandments — and all the more so the eggs; therefore it is said of them, with regard to the Mother, "you shall surely send away the mother." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:3: So too it says (Tikkunei Zohar 21b): but sons are from her innards, of whom it is said (Jeremiah 31:19), "my innards yearn for them" — sons of love from her own womb, and these are the masters of Kabbalah, of whom it is said, "do not take the mother with the sons," for the Mother never departs from them. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:4: The reason that the Mother never departs from them is that they know how to unify the Shechinah in their commandments, their Torah, and their deeds — and the essential of the commandment and the deed is in the completion of the intent; but the chicks, who are masters of Mishnah, their commandments are not complete because of the deficiency of intent. It follows that the all-encompassing rectification for the Shechinah is intent in the commandments, in the Torah, and in all other deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:5: Now, in order to arouse the heart to love the Holy One, blessed be He, one must remember these matters that we shall explain from the words of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, and through this the heart will be aroused to love — although we are yet to state several things that arouse love, nevertheless these particular ones touch on the essence of love for the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and therefore we thought fit to explain them here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:6: It says in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Naso 122a) that repentance [teshuvah] is the Shechinah, who is the final heh, and the intent is that the final heh "returns" [tashuv] to join with Yod-Heh-Vav; and it says afterward: this repentance is called "life," for from her come forth the outflowings of life, which are the souls of Israel — she is the breath that goes out and comes in, into a person's mouth without toil and without labor, the heh with which they were created — and of her it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3), "for by every utterance of the mouth of the Lord does man live" — and she is above a person's head, of her it is said (Numbers 12:8), "and the image of the Lord shall he behold" — "surely man walks about in a mere image" (Psalms 39:7). And because she is above a person's head, it is forbidden for a person to walk four cubits with his head uncovered — for if she departs from over a person's head, life immediately departs from him. And should you say that she likewise rests upon the nations of the world, even though heaven and earth and all their generations were not created for them — she surely does not rest upon them, for Moses asked of the Holy One, blessed be He, that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations of the world, and He granted it to him. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:7: When a person contemplates that the Shechinah is above his head and gives him life, being the soul within him, and likewise the breath by which man is sustained — for existence is impossible in the world without breath, which is the air; and were it not for the air breathing into the wings of the lung, the heart's own fire would burn a person up, as explained in the Tikkunim (28a). And through a person's inhaling of the air, which is the breath of the world, he is sustained — this is "for by every utterance of the mouth of YHVH," which is the breath of the world, coming out of the mouth of YHVH, which is the Shechinah — through her man lives. And this is the heh of "when they were created" [behibar'am, which contains the letters of "Be-Heh bera'am," "with a heh He created them"] — for the heh is breath, since the motion of the heh in its pronunciation is soft, indicating the essence of breath; and just as the Supernal Heh [Binah] is breath, of whom it is said, "for by every utterance of the mouth of YHVH does man live" — for through that very breath the Supernal Man [Adam Elyon] is sustained, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Tazria 47b) — so too through the breath emerging from the Shechinah the lower man is sustained. And therefore, since the life of Israel in particular is through this breath — for the breath that rests upon Israel is not what rests upon the [other] nations, as explained in the passage — and this is "man shall live," and Israel are called "Adam [Man]" — it is fitting to love her and do her will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:8: Especially when one considers how much he has sinned and rebelled against the mouth of the Shechinah, casting off the yoke of her commandments, and she has not burned him in her judgment, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:24), "for the Lord your God is a consuming fire" — and she is called "Righteousness [Tzedek]," a judgment with no leniency at all — nevertheless she pours forth life and breath upon him — it is fitting that he fulfill her commandments and that the fire of her love burn in his heart, until with every single breath he is bound to her, if this be possible — as our sages, of blessed memory, explained in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 14), in these words: Rabbi Bisna, Rabbi Acha, and Rabbi Yochanan, in the name of Rabbi Meir, say: this soul fills the body, and when a person sleeps, it ascends and draws life for him from above. Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chanina: for every single breath a person breathes, he must praise his Creator — why? "Let every neshamah [soul/breath] praise the Lord" (Psalms 150:6) — every single breath shall praise the Lord.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:9: And in the Midrash Rabbah, parashat Vayikra, on the verse "and a soul, when it sins" — they said, in these words: another interpretation, "a soul, when it sins" — this is what Scripture says (Ecclesiastes 6:7), "all the toil of man is for his mouth" — Rabbi Shmuel bar Ami said: what a person has accumulated in commandments and good deeds does not suffice for the breath that goes out of his mouth [i.e., is not enough to repay the debt owed for every breath]. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:10: Further, in Devarim Rabbah, on the verse "and you shall love the Lord your God" — they say, in these words: what is meant by "with all your heart and with all your soul"? With every single soul that He has created within you. Rabbi Meir said: for every single breath a person draws, he is obligated to praise his Maker — from where do we know this? As it is said, "let every neshamah praise the Lord." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:11: Further it is said in the Yerushalmi, chapter "Ein Omdin" (halachah 1), on the verse (Psalms 46:8), "the Lord of hosts is with us," etc.: Rabbi Yosa said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: let this verse never depart from your mouth — "the Lord of hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah." And Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan (Psalms 84:13), "O Lord of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:12: Although there are many particular details in the explanation of these verses, for the great benefit contained in them, the general matter is that one must always place before his eyes the supernal providence, and therefore it says, let this verse never depart from your mouth — for saying "the Lord of hosts is with us" indicates His great love for Israel, that even though YHVH is called "of hosts," being the Prince over the supernal hosts, nevertheless His providence is with us. Further, He is a stronghold and shield to guard us from the mishaps of the world, and this is Selah, without interruption, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Eruvin 54a): wherever "Selah" is said, it has no end forever, as it is said (Psalms 48:9), "as we have heard, so we have seen," etc., "forever, Selah" — and from the redundancy of the phrase "forever, Selah" they proved that wherever Selah is said, it has no end forever.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:13: And even according to Rabbi Abahu's statement, that the verse is "O Lord of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You" — the attribute of trust has many virtues, one of them being that it is impossible for a person to be attached to his God without trust in Him; and when one truly trusts, he is surely attached to YHVH and has no fear of any worldly matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:14: So too the Rashbi explained in the Zohar (parashat Va'era 22a), in these words: another interpretation (Isaiah 26:4), "trust in the Lord forever" — all his days, a person must strengthen himself in the Holy One, blessed be He, for so David said (Psalms 25:2), "my God, in You I have trusted, let me not be ashamed, let not my enemies triumph over me" — and whoever places his trust and strength in Him properly, all the people of the world cannot harm him, for whoever places his strength in the Holy Name is sustained in the world. Why? Because the world is sustained through the Holy Name, this being what is written, "for in Yah, the Lord, is an everlasting Rock" — the Fashioner of worlds. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:15: He explained two matters regarding trust: first, that one must persevere in trust all his days — this is the precision of the word "forever" [adei ad]. Second, that the essence of trust is the strength of clinging to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, "all his days, a person must strengthen himself in the Holy One, blessed be He" — using the word "strengthen" — and likewise below, where it says, "places his trust and strength in Him," which indicates the strength of the grip of clinging, that he cannot be separated from Him, and therefore he trusts in every matter and does not fear the mishaps of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:16: The essence of clinging is to YHVH, as explained in the passage, which says, "because the world is sustained through the Holy Name." The reason is that the Name YHVH is the inward life-force both in this world and in the World to Come — for just as the soul is the life of the body, so this world is the body, and the Name YHVH is the soul within it, and were His life-force, Heaven forbid, to depart from the world, the world would remain formless and void — for His Name, blessed be He, is the soul that sustains everything. Therefore, since a person clings to YHVH, who is the soul, it is fitting that he be sustained in the world all the more, because he continually polishes his soul from the root of the supernal life, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are alive," as I explained in the previous chapter. Thus we have explained the cause that arouses within us love for the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:17: The cause that arouses love for the Holy One, blessed be He, is explained in the Zohar (parashat Terumah 134b), in these words: "from every man whose heart makes him willing you shall take My offering" (Exodus 25:2) — this verse should have simply said "every man whose heart makes him willing"; why "from every man"? Rather, here is a secret for the masters of the [inner] discipline. Happy are these righteous ones who know how to direct their will toward the Supernal Holy King, and all their will is not directed toward this world and the shame of its vanity, but rather they know how to direct their will and cling above, in order to draw down the will of their Master toward them, from above to below. And from what place do they draw that will of their Master, to draw it toward themselves? They draw it from one supernal holy place, from which all holy wills emerge — and who is "every man [kol ish]"? This is the righteous one [Tzaddik/Yesod], who is called "Kol" ["All"], as it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:8), "and the profit of the land is in all [ba-kol]" — therefore "all Your commandments are all [kol]" (Psalms 119:128); "ish" as in "a righteous man [ish tzaddik]" — this is "every man," the master of the house, whose will is always toward the Queen, like a husband who loves his wife, and always "his heart makes him willing" — he loves her, and his heart, which is his Queen, makes willing to cling to him; and although in this great love they are never separated from one another, from that "every man, master of the house" — the master of the Queen — from him "you shall take My offering." It is the way of the world that whoever wishes to take a man's wife from him, he objects and does not let him; but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so — although her whole love is toward Him and His love toward her, from Him they take her, so that she may dwell among them — from that supernal place where all the love of a wife and her husband rests, "you shall take My offering." Happy is the portion of Israel, and happy are all who merit this. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:18: He further says: happy is their portion, that although they take her here, they can do so only with the permission of her husband and with His own permission, and to perform the service of love toward Him — and then, through His own love, "you shall take My offering" — and all this is through those services of prayer and rectification that Israel arrange every day. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:19: Our intent is made clear in this passage: although the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the love of His Shechinah, nevertheless, out of His love for Israel, He gives us permission to draw her near to us below, through prayer and commandments, so that through them she be unified above, and we arouse the love from her toward Him — in the manner of "who chooses His people Israel with love," explained above; and this is what is meant by "to perform the service of love toward Him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:20: However, this passage contains matters that require examination, not all relevant here to the exposition; what is relevant to the exposition of clinging and love we are engaged in is explained in the passage's statement about the rank of the righteous, who know how to strip their thought from materiality and cling with their thought and will to the King of Kings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:21: His words may be understood together with what is said in parashat Bereishit (parashat Bereishit, Heichal Kodesh Kodashim, 45b), which mentions the wills revealed at the time of the supernal union; see there. And all the wills are revealed through the righteous man, who is the one who unites — and there is the essential clinging of the soul of the lower righteous man — as it says: and then that will of all is sweetened, and it is not grasped inward within concealment, and then happy is the portion of one who clings to his Master at that hour — happy is he above, happy is he below; of him it is written (Proverbs 23:25), "let your father and mother rejoice, and let she who bore you exult."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:22: He says further there: whoever merits to cling to his Master in this manner inherits all the worlds, love above, love below. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:23: With this, what is said, "his heart, which is his Queen, makes willing to cling to him," may be understood — because through him the supernal will is revealed to her, as explained, and she is illuminated by the light of the Infinite, and this is the reality of the union, and this is His love toward her, in the secret of "and a river goes out of Eden to water the garden" — for if there were no garden, where would the river's flow and watering go? This is what my master, may his rest be in Eden, explained in Sefer HaPardes, that the supernal beings need the lower beings. And through "you shall take My offering" and unifying her in those services of prayer, you are bound to the supernal will revealed in the union, as explained — and thus the whole passage is found to be connected as one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:24: We find ourselves taught that all clinging depends on the rectifications of prayer, which are all rectifications and unifications of the Shechinah; and we find ourselves taught that the essence of clinging and love depends on stripping the thought from the desires of this world, all of whose desires are nullified in death, as is known — and the essential thing is to cling one's soul to the supernal will. And the essential thing to know is all the unifications and the whole reality of divine service: that there is no difference between us and Him, blessed be He, though He is exalted, high above the high — He is with us, watching over the particulars that are far too exalted for such attention; and there is no difference except from the side of sin, as it is said (Isaiah 59:2), "your iniquities have separated," etc. However, when a person repents, he is bound to his Creator — the proof of which is when you examine what we wrote in the previous chapters, of how many miracles were performed for Israel, and the Holy One, blessed be He, performs [miracles] with us always and answers us in our time of distress.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:25: Especially when a person contemplates the rank of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the other Tanna'im, whose words would be fulfilled immediately, at times even unintentionally, as in the matter of "it happened as though inadvertently, from before the ruler," etc., mentioned several times in the Gemara (Mo'ed Katan 18a), and in the Zohar in parashat Vayechi (218a): "Master of the universe, Rabbi Yitzchak has become known to us" [uttered spontaneously and fulfilled] — and many such miracles brought in the Zohar. Therefore, when a person considers this matter, he will see that there is no barrier at all between him and holiness, and therefore he is obligated to serve the Creator like one who serves a king, standing before him and performing the supernal will according to the changes of the order of supernal governance in the times of day and night and the other times — so should he perform his service in his prayer and his Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:26: First, it is fitting that a person set his attention every day to unify the Shechinah in the three prayers, Shacharit, Minchah, and Ma'ariv. The reason for these three times is that as the lower time changes, so the supernal governance changes — to Chesed, to Din, and to Rachamim — and therefore in the morning we arouse Chesed. And similarly, our sages, of blessed memory, explained in Bereishit Rabbah, parashat Vayetze (68:9), the reason for the three prayers: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said there, the patriarchs instituted the three prayers — Abraham instituted the morning prayer, etc. And it further says: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said, corresponding to the three times the day changes — in the evening one should say, "may it be Your will, O Lord my God, that You bring me out from darkness to light"; in the morning one should say, "I thank You before You, O Lord my God, that You have brought me out from darkness to light"; at Minchah one should say, "may it be Your will, O Lord my God, that just as You have granted me to see the sun in its rising, so You grant me to see it in its setting." The Rabbis say: they instituted them corresponding to the daily offerings. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:27: If so, it follows that as the time changes, so the praise and thanksgiving to the Name is obligated because of the good He has bestowed — and in order that one be complete in loving the Name and pray with a passionate heart, remembering the good He does for him, the prayers were instituted at different times.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:28: Similarly, it is explained in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 28:1) on (Ecclesiastes 1:5), "and the sun rises and the sun sets" — in these words: Rabbi Levi said, all that people gather of commandments and good deeds in this world suffices for the Holy One, blessed be He, to make the sun rise for them, as it is said, "and the sun rises and the sun sets."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:29: At the time he awakens from his sleep, if he rises early to study Torah out of love for the Shechinah, how good is his portion, as we shall elaborate on its greatness with God's help. This the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Va'era 30a), in these words: come and see, when the King comes to His bed, at the time midnight is divided, the north wind is aroused — this arouses affection toward the Queen, for were it not for the arousal of the north, the King would not join with her, because the north dwells in affection, as it is said (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," while the south embraces in love, as it is written, "and his right hand embraces me." Then how many joyful ones arouse song, until morning comes, as it is written (Job 38:7), "when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy"; and when morning comes, all the upper and lower beings say song, and Israel, in a similar manner, below, as it is written (Isaiah 62:6), "you who make mention of the Lord, keep not silence" — "keep not silence" precisely at night — when midnight is divided, those whose longing is to constantly make mention of the Holy One, blessed be He, give their heart no rest, and stand to make mention of the Holy One, blessed be He; when morning comes they rise early to the synagogue and praise the Holy One, blessed be He, and so too after midday, and so too at night when it darkens and night clings to darkness, and the sun sets — of these it is written, "you who make mention of the Lord, keep not silence" — and this is the holy people of Israel. — end of quotation.
